newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine scraps 10 percent import duty on raw sugar.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine scraps 10 percent import duty on raw sugar.

text.p: Ukraine has scrapped a 10 percent tax on raw sugar imports, a top official at the national sugar producers' association said on Tuesday.

"The government limited raw imports to protect its own sugar industry. Now that the refining season is over, the law (which imposed the tax) is no longer in effect," said the official from UkrSukor, formerly the state sugar concern and now called the National Association of Ukrainian Sugar Producers.
The tax was introduced in November 1996.
Ukraine produced 561,000 tonnes of refined sugar from raws imported last year, up from about 300,000 tonnes in 1995.
Its total 1996 refined sugar output, from all sources, was 3.26 million tonnes.

The former Soviet republic, which regularly produced two million tonnes of white sugar from Cuban raws a year in the Soviet era, has been working to rebuild its sugar refining industry based on raws while supporting local beet producers.
A Western trader said that the tax on raw sugar imports had sent all of Ukraine's raw refining business to Russia.
"This was a very bad move," he said.
But he said scrapping the tax would not help things until Ukraine repealed a second rule that sugar refined from raws must designate the country from which the raws were imported.
Another trader said the practice of refining sugar from raws in Ukraine was no longer worth the trouble.
"Tolling operations that used to take place are no longer successful or profitable," he said.
